topicName: Production Monitoring, Log Analysis (Kibana/Splunk), and Triage
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Production Monitoring, Log Analysis (Kibana/Splunk), and Triage in Manual Testing"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial bridges the gap between manual quality assurance and production operations. While manual testers typically validate features in staging environments, modern QA strategies require proficiency in production monitoring, log analysis tools like Kibana and Splunk, and systematic triage when production incidents occur."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding Production Monitoring for Manual Testers"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Production monitoring involves observing system health, user traffic, and application metrics in a live environment. As a manual tester, understanding dashboards helps you verify if a deployed bug fix is functioning correctly or if an unexpected error spike correlates with your recent feature release."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Key metrics to monitor: HTTP 5xx and 4xx error rates, API response times, CPU and memory utilization, and transaction failure rates."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Correlation: Linking a reported UI bug in production to specific metric anomalies on monitoring dashboards like Datadog or New Relic."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Log Analysis using Kibana (Elasticsearch)"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Kibana is the visualization layer for the ELK stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana). Manual testers can use Kibana to trace user sessions, verify payload structures, and extract exact stack traces when reproducing intermittent bugs."},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"To find specific errors in Kibana, use Elasticsearch Query Language (KQL) in the discover tab. Here is an example query to filter for critical checkout failures during a specific timeframe:"},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"service.name: \"checkout-service\" AND log.level: \"ERROR\" AND http.response.status_code: 500"},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use the transaction ID or correlation ID generated during your manual test run to filter out unrelated system noise."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Inspect the JSON document structure of the log to verify if the frontend sent the correct parameters to the backend API."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Log Analysis using Splunk"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Splunk is a powerful log management and SIEM platform. It uses Search Processing Language (SPL) to query machine data. Testers can leverage Splunk to audit user actions, view database query performance, and trace asynchronous background jobs."},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Consider a scenario where a user reports that login is failing intermittently. You can run the following SPL query in Splunk to investigate user authentication failures:"},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"index=\"production_logs\" sourcetype=\"auth_service\" action=\"login\" status=\"failure\" | stats count by user_id, error_message"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Look for patterns in error messages to determine if failures are browser-specific, network-related, or tied to invalid data payloads."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Compare successful login log sequences with failed login log sequences to identify missing headers or tokens."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Systematic Incident Triage for Manual Testers"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Triage is the process of prioritizing and investigating bugs to determine their root cause, severity, and impacted audience. When a production issue is flagged, manual testers play a crucial role in the triage workflow."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 1: Reproduceability Check. Attempt to reproduce the issue in a lower environment (Staging/QA) using the exact steps and user profiles identified in production."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 2: Log Extraction. Pull relevant logs from Kibana or Splunk, attaching timestamps, user IDs, and error stack traces to the bug ticket."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 3: Impact Analysis. Determine how many users are affected by checking transaction volumes on monitoring tools."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 4: Component Assignment. Route the ticket to the correct engineering team (frontend, backend, database, or DevOps) based on log evidence."},{"order":25,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary"},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"By mastering production monitoring dashboards and log query languages like KQL and SPL, manual testers evolve from simple user-interface validators into comprehensive quality engineers who can effectively troubleshoot, triage, and accelerate the resolution of critical production defects."}]
